build_system: pip install from requirements.txt, deployed via Railway (Procfile)
test_framework: No test framework; syntax validation via AST parse
verification_instructions: Run python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('bot.py').read())" to verify no syntax errors
setup_instructions: pip install -r requirements.txt (only needed for import validation)
environment_constraints: OPEN_INTERNET - full network access. Single-file bot (bot.py, 9248 lines).
contribution_requirements: All code in bot.py. Reply Keyboard only for users. No inline keyboards for user navigation.

key_patterns.buttons: All button texts use _b() helper for Unicode bold conversion
key_patterns.keyboards: _kb() wraps ReplyKeyboardMarkup construction; rows are lists of button texts
key_patterns.formatters: fmt_* functions format messages. Currently some use _card() (box-drawing) which needs to be replaced with simple _SEP-based formatting
key_patterns.states: UserFlow and AdminFlow StatesGroup classes define FSM states
key_patterns.handlers: router_start for user handlers, router_admin for admin handlers, router_global for Home button
key_patterns.separator: _SEP = '━' * 22 is the standard separator; _LINE = '─' * 22 for sub-separators
key_patterns.settings: SETTINGS_MAP dict maps button text to (key, type, prompt); SETTINGS_CATEGORIES groups them into sub-categories

directory_structure: Single-file project: bot.py is the entire application. requirements.txt for deps. Procfile/railway.toml for deployment.
